- When sentiment is consistently high (≥0.67) over recent days, model tends to overestimate prices; reduce forecast slightly, especially after spikes.
- If sentiment is low (≤0.33) and prices are trending down, model often underestimates; adjust upward to reflect mean reversion or sentiment-driven support.
- After a sharp price spike, model frequently overshoots in the next few days; apply a “cool-down” correction by reducing forecast by 1–3% for the following 3–5 days.
- When sentiment is mixed or volatile (alternating 0.33–0.67), model exhibits erratic behavior; smooth transitions and avoid large swings in forecast unless sentiment confirms direction.
- Model tends to overreact to short-term sentiment shifts; for horizon >10 days, apply a 1–2% downward bias if sentiment is negative or neutral.
- If sentiment is uniformly positive and price is near historical mean, model often overpredicts; cap forecast at 1–2% above recent 7-day average to avoid overextension.
- For 30-day forecasts, if sentiment is consistently positive and price is rising, model may overestimate; apply a 1–3% downward adjustment to align with sentiment-driven mean reversion.
